state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It seems like you're trying to apply proportional changes to the heights of the plants. Think about what happens to the range when all values are changed by the same proportion. Can you identify how the range might be affected in each scenario? Remember, the range is determined by the difference between the highest and lowest values.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you mean about the range being the difference between the highest and lowest values. So if Tom cuts everything in half, the highest and lowest would also be cut in half, right? But I'm not sure how that affects the range. And with Katie, if she adds \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) to each plant, wouldn't that just make everything taller but still keep the same difference between the tallest and shortest? I'm a bit confused about how that works.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It's great that you're thinking about how the changes affect the highest and lowest values. Remember that the range is determined by the difference between those two values. Think about how cutting the heights in half or adding \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) to each plant might impact that difference. Keep exploring and you're on the right track!

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeatedly prompts the student to think about the range without directly addressing the proportional change misconception, and by Turn 2 the student actually articulates the correct reasoning for Katie's scenario but remains confused, suggesting the scaffolding is insufficient to resolve the misconception.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides general prompts about the range concept but fails to break the problem into manageable steps, offer scaffolded support adjusted to the student's specific confusion, or guide them through either scenario systematically despite the student explicitly expressing confusion about how the operations affect the range.
